response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(E.`aCL IgM`) AS v FROM Examination E JOIN Patient P ON E.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), d AS (SELECT ID, SEX, v, v - (SELECT AVG(v) FROM p) AS dev FROM p), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS ad FROM d GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.v AS `aCL IgM`, d.dev AS deviation, d.dev - s.ad AS excess_over_sex_avg FROM d JOIN s ON d.SEX = s.SEX WHERE d.dev > s.ad ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Patients with a NULL SEX are dropped, because the sex-group join uses equality and NULL matches nothing. A blank SEX is its own group.
Patients whose examinations all have NULL aCL IgM have a NULL per-patient value. They are ignored in the overall mean and never pass the 'above average' filter.
